verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy the brother,
verses.1:2: to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ in Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying for you,
verses.1:4: having heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and the love that you have toward all the saints
verses.1:5: because of the hope stored up for you in the heavens, of which you heard beforehand in the word of the truth of the gospel
verses.1:6: which has come to you, just as in all the world also it is bearing fruit and growing, just as it also is among you, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
verses.1:7: just as you learned from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of Christ on our behalf,
verses.1:8: who also made known to us your love in the Spirit.
verses.1:9: For this reason we also, from the day we heard, do not cease praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the full knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
verses.1:10: so as to walk in a manner worthy of the Lord, to please Him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the full knowledge of God,
verses.1:11: being empowered with all power according to the might of His glory, for all endurance and patience with joy,
verses.1:12: giving thanks to the Father, who qualified you for the share of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
verses.1:13: who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
verses.1:14: in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
verses.1:15: This One is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of all creation,
verses.1:16: because in Him all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through Him and for Him.
verses.1:17: And He Himself is before all things, and in Him all things hold together,
verses.1:18: and He Himself is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, firstborn from the dead, so that in all things He Himself might hold first place,
verses.1:19: because in Him all the fullness was pleased to dwell,
verses.1:20: and through Him to reconcile all things to Him, having made peace through the blood of His cross—through Him, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens.
verses.1:21: And you, who were once alienated and enemies in your mind in evil deeds—
verses.1:22: yet now you have been reconciled in the body of His flesh through death—to present you holy and blameless and beyond reproach before Him,
verses.1:23: if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and not shifting away from the hope of the gospel that you heard, which was proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a servant.
verses.1:24: Now I rejoice in my sufferings on your behalf, and in my flesh I fill up what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ on behalf of His body, which is the church,
verses.1:25: of which I became a servant according to the stewardship of God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
verses.1:26: the mystery that has been hidden from the ages and from the generations—but now it has been revealed to His saints,
verses.1:27: to whom God willed to make known what the wealth of the glory of this mystery is among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
verses.1:28: Him we proclaim, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person mature in Christ.
verses.1:29: For this I also labor, striving according to His working that works in me with power.
verses.2:1: For I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you and those in Laodicea, and all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
verses.2:2: so that their hearts may be encouraged, knit together in love and into all the wealth of the full assurance of understanding, into the full knowledge of the mystery of God, Christ,
verses.2:3: in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
verses.2:4: I say this so that no one may delude you with persuasive speech.
verses.2:5: For even though I am absent in the flesh, yet in the spirit I am with you, rejoicing and seeing your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
verses.2:6: Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in Him,
verses.2:7: having been rooted and being built up in Him and being established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
verses.2:8: Watch out that no one takes you captive through philosophy and empty deceit, according to human tradition, according to the elementary principles of the world, and not according to Christ.
verses.2:9: For in Him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
verses.2:10: and you have been brought to fullness in Him, who is the head of every ruler and authority,
verses.2:11: in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ,
verses.2:12: having been buried with Him in baptism, in which you were also raised with Him through faith in the working of God, who raised Him from the dead.
verses.2:13: And you, who were dead in trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh—He made you alive together with Him, having forgiven us all our trespasses,
verses.2:14: having wiped out the handwritten record of debt against us with its decrees, which was hostile to us; and He has taken it out of the way, having nailed it to the cross.
verses.2:15: Having disarmed the rulers and the authorities, He made an open display of them, triumphing over them in Him.
verses.2:16: Therefore let no one judge you in food and in drink, or with regard to a feast or a new moon or Sabbaths,
verses.2:17: which are a shadow of the things to come, but the substance belongs to Christ.
verses.2:18: Let no one disqualify you, delighting in humility and the worship of angels, entering into the things he has seen, puffed up without reason by the mind of his flesh,
verses.2:19: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, being supplied and knit together through the joints and ligaments, grows with a growth from God.
verses.2:20: If you died with Christ to the elementary principles of the world, why, as though living in the world, do you submit to decrees,
verses.2:21: "Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch"
verses.2:22: —all of which are destined for decay through use—according to human commands and teachings?
verses.2:23: Such things indeed have an appearance of wisdom in self-imposed worship and humility and harsh treatment of the body, yet they are of no value against the gratification of the flesh.
verses.3:1: Therefore, if you were raised together with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, sitting at the right hand of God.
verses.3:2: Keep your minds on the things above, not on the things on the earth.
verses.3:3: For you died, and your life has been hidden with Christ in God.
verses.3:4: When Christ, your life, is manifested, then you also will be manifested with Him in glory.
verses.3:5: Therefore, put to death the members that are on the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry,
verses.3:6: on account of which the wrath of God is coming,
verses.3:7: in which you also once walked when you were living in these things.
verses.3:8: But now you also put away all these things: wrath, fury, malice, slander, and obscene speech from your mouth.
verses.3:9: Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self together with its practices,
verses.3:10: and have put on the new self, which is being renewed to full knowledge according to the image of the One who created it,
verses.3:11: where there is not Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free; rather, Christ is all and in all.
verses.3:12: Therefore, as chosen ones of God, holy and beloved, put on hearts of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience,
verses.3:13: bearing with one another and forgiving each other if anyone has a complaint against another; just as the Lord also forgave you, so you also must do.
verses.3:14: And over all these things put on love, which is the bond of perfection.
verses.3:15: And let the peace of Christ govern in your hearts, to which you were also called in one body; and be grateful.
verses.3:16: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs in grace, singing in your hearts to God.
verses.3:17: And whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all things in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
verses.3:18: Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
verses.3:19: Husbands, love your wives and do not become bitter toward them.
verses.3:20: Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is well-pleasing in the Lord.
verses.3:21: Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they may not lose heart.
verses.3:22: Slaves, obey your masters according to the flesh in all things, not in acts of eye-service as people-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing the Lord.
verses.3:23: Whatever you do, work from the soul, as for the Lord and not for people,
verses.3:24: knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. You serve the Lord Christ.
verses.3:25: For the one who does wrong will receive back the wrong he did, and there is no partiality.
verses.4:1: Masters, provide what is just and fair to your slaves, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.
verses.4:2: Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving,
verses.4:3: praying at the same time for us as well, that God may open for us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, on account of which I have also been bound,
verses.4:4: so that I may make it manifest as I ought to speak.
verses.4:5: Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the opportunity.
verses.4:6: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you know how you ought to answer each individual.
verses.4:7: Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful servant and fellow slave in the Lord, will make known to you all the things concerning me.
verses.4:8: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know how things are with us and that he may encourage your hearts,
verses.4:9: together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all the things here.
verses.4:10: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, welcome him),
verses.4:11: and Jesus who is called Justus. Of those who are of the circumcision, these alone are fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have become a comfort to me.
verses.4:12: Epaphras, who is one of you, a slave of Christ Jesus, greets you, always striving on your behalf in his prayers, so that you may stand complete and fully assured in all the will of God.
verses.4:13: For I bear witness for him that he has much toil on your behalf and for those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
verses.4:14: Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, as well as Demas.
verses.4:15: Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nympha and the church in her house.
verses.4:16: And when this letter has been read among you, see to it that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you also read the one from Laodicea.
verses.4:17: And say to Archippus, "See to the ministry that you received in the Lord, so that you fulfill it."
verses.4:18: The greeting is by my own hand—Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.

notes.1:7: Some Greek manuscripts read "on your behalf" (hyper hymon) instead of "on our behalf" (hyper hemon).
notes.1:15: Greek prōtotokos ("firstborn") can denote priority in time or preeminence in rank.
notes.1:19: The Greek has no separate subject for "was pleased"; "all the fullness" may be the subject, or "God" may be understood ("God was pleased for all the fullness to dwell in Him").
notes.1:22: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the passive "you have been reconciled" (apokatellagete), forming a parenthetical break in syntax; other manuscripts read the active "He has reconciled" (apokatellaxen).
notes.1:24: The genitive in "the afflictions of Christ" may denote afflictions Christ Himself endured or afflictions borne for Him or in union with Him.
notes.2:8: The Greek stoicheia ("elementary principles") can refer either to foundational teachings and religious rudiments or to elemental spiritual powers governing the cosmos (likewise in 2:20).
notes.2:14: The Greek cheirographon refers to a handwritten certificate of debt, used metaphorically for the binding record of obligation standing against humanity.
notes.2:15: The final phrase "in Him" (referring to Christ) can also be rendered "by it" (referring to the cross in v. 14).
notes.2:18: The phrase "entering into the things he has seen" (ha heoraken embateuon) is difficult and may refer to initiation into visionary experiences or delving into claimed visions; some later manuscripts insert a negative ("things he has not seen").
notes.2:23: The final clause is grammatically ambiguous and may mean either that ascetic practices have no value in restraining fleshly gratification or that they have no true worth and serve only to gratify the flesh.
notes.3:6: The Greek text here lacks "upon the sons of disobedience," which many manuscripts add (compare Ephesians 5:6).
notes.3:15: The verb rendered "govern" literally means "act as umpire" or "arbitrate."
notes.3:16: Punctuation is debated: "in all wisdom" may modify either "dwell" (as punctuated here) or "teaching and admonishing," and "in grace" may also mean "with gratitude."
notes.3:24: The Greek verb form can be read either as an indicative ("You serve the Lord Christ") or as an imperative ("Serve the Lord Christ").
notes.4:1: Greek uses the same word (kyrios) for both earthly "masters" and the heavenly "Master" (Lord).
notes.4:8: Some manuscripts read "that he may know how things are with you," while the critical text reads "that you may know how things are with us."
notes.4:15: Following the feminine pronoun "her" in the critical text, the name is feminine Nympha; other manuscripts read masculine "his" (Nymphas) or plural "their."
notes.4:16: The letter from Laodicea is not preserved under that name; some scholars identify it with Ephesians (as a circular letter) or with a lost Pauline letter.
